title: Jesus our groom part 5
scripture_text: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God believe also in me. My Father’s house has many rooms; if that were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you? And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me that you also may be where I am. You know the way to the place where I am going.” Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going, so how can we know the way?” Jesus answered, ‘I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you really know me, you will know my Father as well. From now on, you do know him and have seen him. Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father and that will be enough for us.” Jesus answered: “Don’t you know me, Philip, even after I have been among you such a long time? Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you I do not speak on my own authority. Rather, it is the Father, living in me, who is doing his work. Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or at least believe on the evidence of the works themselves. Very truly I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father. And I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. You may ask me for anything in my name, and I will do it.’’
devotional:
Knowing the Father is the essence of intimacy. John’s gospel is a gospel about the father. In chapters 13-17 there are 50 references to the father, and in verses 6-13 of our chapter there are 12 references; there is an intensity, a depth, a depiction of the kind of father God is and the kind of father he wants us to enjoy.

John 14:10 says. ‘Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you I do not speak on my own authority. Rather, it is the Father, living in me, who is doing his work. Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or at least believe on the evidence of the works themselves.’

These are very weighty theological verses that contain a lot of truth about the Godhead. However in their essence, Jesus is describing the kind of relationship his Father has with him, and the kind of relationship he would love to have with us.

I realise that Jesus’ relationship with his father was unique and special. However, the relationship the father had with his son models the kind of relationship he wants to have with us. So when Jesus speaks about being the way to the father, he is speaking more about it being a transformational process of becoming more like children of God than about a geographical location.

Jesus going to his father will make the work he has called us to possible.

John 14:12 ‘Very truly I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.’

This is one of those verses that has caused a lot of debate and confusion. We need to keep these words in their context. Jesus is still speaking as a ‘groom’ who is about to return to his Father. Because he is returning to his father by defeating Satan, sin and death, the works that we will do will reflect his glorious victory. Some Christians teach that Jesus is saying that we will do greater miracles than him.

This is unlikely for a number of reasons:-

a. When Jesus said: - ‘I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these.’ Whoever believes includes all believers. Contrast this to what Paul says in 1 Corinthians 12:10, speaking about the gifts of the Spirit. to another [some] miraculous powers, to another prophecy to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in different kinds of tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues. So everyone cannot do miracles, but all can do the ‘greater works.’

b. In John’s gospel the word that he uses for miracles is signs, not work or things.

c. I doubt if anyone could do the miracles Jesus did.

I think the point is this, the greater works are the glories of the father being clearly displayed through his family because of Jesus’ victory.

5. Jesus going to the father redefines prayer.

Look at these amazing verses. John 14:13-14 ‘And I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. You may ask me for anything in my name, and I will do it.’

‘Our Father, In heaven, hallowed be your name.’

Having a genuine desire to bring God glory is only possible in the context of growing intimacy with him.

When Jesus tells us that He is the way, He is inviting us to embark on a life-long pursuit of an intimate relationship with Him. He being the way, means that our future, our plans, hopes and dreams are all tied up in our relationship with Him.
prayer: Father may I live an intimate life with you so I can bring you glory.
